title: Identifying an anonymous user merges their properties
means: When an anonymous user is identified as User A, all the properties of the anonymous user are added to User A, following the property conflict rule above. The page example starts with User A (name User A, location London, timezone GMT), sets name Anonymous User and phone 0800-POSTHOG on the anonymous user, and identifies user_A with timezone GMT+8; name and location stay with User A and phone is added.

title: An anonymous person can be identified before an identified person exists
means: As soon as you are able, typically when a user logs in or creates an account, you call identify on the frontend with a distinct_id. This merges the anonymous person into the identified person, linking the two IDs together.

title: An already identified alias is refused while its event is ingested
means: The alias_id must not have been previously used as the distinct_id argument of an identify() or alias() call. When calling either of these with invalid inputs, we process the event normally; merging users will be refused and the event will only be tied to the user associated with distinct_id.

title: The property page second capture overwrites name only
means: name: 'Mr. Fox'; initial_url: '/blog'. Using set replaces any property value that may have been set on a person profile. In contrast, set_once only sets the property if it has never been set before.

title: A request body over 20MB is refused
means: The entire request body must be less than 20MB by default: the server reads a body up to BATCH_BODY_SIZE (20,971,520 bytes, rust/capture/src/router.rs) and refuses a longer one before decoding it, 413 with maximum event size exceeded: Request body exceeds limit of 20971520 bytes (rust/capture/src/extractors.rs, api.rs).

title: Flags page basic request
means: Use this endpoint when you only need to evaluate feature flags. It returns a response with just the flag evaluation results: flags, errorsWhileComputingFlags and requestId. The page's answer evaluates three flags its project holds; a project holding none answers flags as an empty object.

title: Flags page request with configuration
